Model#

class imbal.regression.Model(*args, **kwargs)#

Bases: Model

Package location: imbal.regression.Model

An extension of Keras’s Model class that can perform alternative types of model fits which aim to address common issues when applying machine learning algorithms to imbalanced/long-tail data.

This imbal.regression.Model class is intended for use only on regression problems.

For a comparison of how these fit methods perform compared to a standard fit on imbalanced/long-tail data, see the information at the bottom of this page.

balanced_fit(x=None, y=None, sample_density=None, sample_weight=None, validation_data=None, validation_densities=None, validation_split=None, batch_size=32, shuffle=True, stratify_batches=False, **kwargs)#

Performs a density-balanced fit, where by default, each instance is equally weighted in a manner that is inversely proportional to the instance’s probability density during the model fitting process.

Parameters:

  • x – Optional, default None (Same as model.fit). A NumPy array of data points, arranged as a column vector

  • y –

    Optional, default None (Same as model.fit).

  • sample_weight – Optional, default None. A list of sample weights. If specified, overrides sample_density.

  • sample_density – Optional, default None. A list of sample probability densities. If unspecified, sample_weight must be specified.

  • validation_data –

    Optional, default None (Same as model.fit). The data used to validate the model during training. See Tensorflow’s model.fit documentation.

  • validation_densities – : Optional, default None. A list of sample probability densities for the provided validation_data. Only required if validation_data is provided without sample weights.

  • validation_split – Optional, default None. A float value representing the proportion of the provided training data to split off into a separate dataset used for model validation.

  • batch_size –

    Optional, default None (Same as model.fit). The batch size to use during training.

  • shuffle –

    Optional, default True (Same as model.fit). Whether to shuffle the data before each epoch.

  • stratify_batches – Optional, default True. Whether to stratify data batch-wise during training. See DatasetWithBatching for details. Only used when multi_output is True.

  • **kwargs – Any additional keyword arguments accepted by TensorFlow’s model.fit function

Returns:

A History object. Its History.history attribute is a record of training loss values and metrics values at successive epochs, as well as validation loss values and validation metrics values (if applicable).

Example:

# Assume regression data is already loaded in '(x_train, y_train), (x_test, y_test)'

input_shape = x_train.shape[1:]
inputs = keras.Input(shape=input_shape)
x = layers.Dense(18, activation='relu')(inputs)
x = layers.Dense(9, activation='relu')(x)
x = layers.Flatten()(x)
x = layers.Dense(6, activation='relu')(x)
x = layers.Flatten()(x)
output = layers.Dense(1)(x)

model =  imbal.regression.Model(inputs=inputs, outputs=output)

model.compile(
    loss="mse",
    optimizer=keras.optimizers.Adam(learning_rate=1e-4),
    metrics=["mse"]
)

kde_bandwidth = imbal.regression.fit_kde(
    y_train,
    bin_count=32
)
densities = imbal.regression.get_sample_densities(
    y_train,
    kde_bandwidth
)

model.balanced_fit(
    x_train,
    y_train,
    sample_density=densities,
    validation_split=0.2
)
rRT_fit(x=None, y=None, sample_weight=None, sample_density=None, validation_data=None, validation_split=None, validation_densities=None, epochs=1, batch_size=32, shuffle=True, stratify_batches=False, **kwargs)#

Performs a regressor re-training (rRT) fit, inspired by the classifier re-training (cRT) method as described in this paper by Kang et al. (ICLR 2020).

Parameters:

  • x –

    Optional, default None (Same as model.fit). A Numpy array of data points, arranged as a column vector

  • y –

    Optional, default None (Same as model.fit). A Numpy array of labels, arranged as a row vector, column vector, or list of one-hot vectors.

  • sample_weight – Optional, default None. A Numpy array of sample weights.

  • sample_density – Optional, default None. A list of sample probability densities. If unspecified, sample_weight must be specified.

  • validation_data –

    Optional, default None (Same as model.fit). The data used to validate the model during training. See Tensorflow’s model.fit documentation.

  • validation_densities – : Optional, default None. A list of sample probability densities for the provided validation_data. Only required if validation_data is provided without sample weights.

  • validation_split – Optional, default None. A float value representing the proportion of the provided training data to split off into a separate dataset used for model validation.

  • epochs –

    Optional, default 1 (Same as model.fit). The number of epochs to train for. If an int, the provided number of epochs will be used during the first stage, and halved for the second stage. If a tuple or list of length 2, the value in the first index will be used as the number of epochs in the first stage of training, and the second index for the number of epochs in the second stage of training.

  • batch_size –

    Optional, default 32 (Same as model.fit). The batch size to use during training.

  • shuffle –

    Optional, default True (Same as model.fit). Whether to shuffle the data before each epoch.

  • stratify_batches – Optional, default True. Whether to stratify data batch-wise during training. See DatasetWithBatching for details.

  • **kwargs –

    Any additional keyword arguments accepted by TensorFlow’s model.fit function

Returns:

A tuple (s1, s2) of History objects. Its History.history attribute is a record of training loss values and metrics values at successive epochs, as well as validation loss values and validation metrics values (if applicable).

Example:

# Assume regression data is already loaded in '(x_train, y_train), (x_test, y_test)'

input_shape = x_train.shape[1:]
inputs = keras.Input(shape=input_shape)
x = layers.Dense(18, activation='relu')(inputs)
x = layers.Dense(9, activation='relu')(x)
x = layers.Flatten()(x)
x = layers.Dense(6, activation='relu')(x)
x = layers.Flatten()(x)
output = layers.Dense(1)(x)

model =  imbal.regression.Model(inputs=inputs, outputs=output)

model.compile(
    loss="mse",
    optimizer=keras.optimizers.Adam(learning_rate=1e-4),
    metrics=["mse"],
    representation_layer_index=-2
)

kde_bandwidth = imbal.regression.fit_kde(
    y_train,
    bin_count=32
)
densities = imbal.regression.get_sample_densities(
    y_train,
    kde_bandwidth
)

model.rRT_fit(
    x_train,
    y_train,
    sample_density=densities,
    validation_split=0.2
)
compile(generate_decoder_branch=False, representation_layer_index=-2, **kwargs)#

An extension of TensorFlow’s model.compile function, which takes all the same parameters as the original function, along with some additional parameters used by the additional functionalities provided by this extended model class.

Includes the ability to optionally generate a decoder branch extending from the provided model, which aids in achieving a better representation space, usually resulting in better performance on imbalanced data. This feature can be enabled by setting generate_decoder_branch to True. (see imbal.util.generate_decoder for more details).

Note: generate_decoder_branch is off by default due to its experimental nature, but it may be worth using if your model fits the anticipated structure.

Parameters:

  • generate_decoder_branch – Optional, default False. Whether to generate a decoder branch for the purpose of training the model.

  • representation_layer_index – Optional, default -2. The layer from which the weights of all layers prior are frozen during the second stage of the decoupled training. Also, when generated_decoder_branch is True, the index of the layer from which the decoder branch in generated.

  • **kwargs –

    Any keyword arguments accepted by TensorFlow’s model.compile function

Returns:

None

fit(x=None, y=None, sample_weight=None, validation_data=None, validation_split=None, batch_size=32, shuffle=True, stratify_batches=False, **kwargs)#

An extension of TensorFlow’s model.fit function that allows for data batches to be stratified if desired.

Parameters:

  • x –

    Optional, default None (Same as model.fit). A NumPy array of data points, arranged as a column vector

  • y –

    Optional, default None (Same as model.fit). A NumPy array of labels, arranged as a row vector, column vector, or list of one-hot vectors.

  • sample_weight – Optional, default None. A list of sample weights. If specified, overrides class_weights.

  • validation_data –

    Optional, default None (Same as model.fit). The data used to validate the model during training. See Tensorflow’s model.fit documentation.

  • validation_split – Optional, default None. A float value representing the proportion of the provided training data to split off into a separate dataset used for model validation.

  • batch_size –

    Optional, default None (Same as model.fit). The batch size to use during training.

  • shuffle –

    Optional, default True (Same as model.fit). Whether to shuffle the data before each epoch.

  • stratify_batches – Optional, default True. Whether to stratify data batch-wise during training. See DatasetWithBatching for details. Only used when multi_output is True.

  • **kwargs –

    Any additional keyword arguments accepted by TensorFlow’s model.fit function

Returns:

A History object. Its History.history attribute is a record of training loss values and metrics values at successive epochs, as well as validation loss values and validation metrics values (if applicable).

override_second_stage_fit_parameters(**kwargs)#

Used to optionally override the parameters passed to the second stage of a decoupled fit. For instance, if you wanted to use a callback during the second stage of a decoupled fit, but not the first, you can call override_second_stage_fit_parameters before calling the decoupled fit`, specifying a callback in override_second_stage_fit_parameters but not in the fit call.

Parameters:

**kwargs –

Any keyword arguments accepted by TensorFlow’s model.fit function

Returns:

None
